note: Shared glossary of Italian driving words. 'en' = short meaning, 'note' = plain-English explanation for beginners.

terms.note: Passing a vehicle that is moving in your same direction. In Italy you normally overtake on the left.
The verb for 'sorpasso'.
Used for passing a vehicle, and also for going over a limit (superare i limiti = exceed the limits).
The vehicle that is being passed.
Who is allowed to go first. 'Dare precedenza' = give way.
Let the other road user go first.
The part of the road where vehicles drive. It does not include the pavement or the hard shoulder.
On a two-way road: the half used by one direction of traffic.
A road split into two roads, one per direction, with a barrier or strip in between (like a dual carriageway).
A strip of the carriageway wide enough for one line of vehicles.
The lane on the left used for passing.
The extra lane used to speed up and join a motorway or fast road.
The extra lane used to slow down before leaving a motorway or fast road.
The lane at the side of a motorway, only for emergencies.
A lane only for some vehicles, for example buses or taxis.
The direction the traffic is moving in.
Vehicles drive in both directions on the same road.
All vehicles drive in the same direction.
Traffic coming towards you.
The right-hand side of the carriageway.
The line in the middle of a two-way road.
A continuous white line. You must not cross it.
A dashed white line. You may cross it when it is safe.
Same as 'striscia discontinua': it can be crossed.
The strip at the side of the carriageway, outside it.
A place where roads meet or cross.
Where two roads cross.
A place where the road turns. You often cannot see far ahead.
A rise in the road. You cannot see what is behind it.
How far you can see. 'Scarsa visibilità' = poor visibility (fog, heavy rain, night).
Slowing down or blocking other road users.
A situation where an accident could happen.
An action while driving, like overtaking, turning or parking.
The flashing lights ('frecce') that show you are turning or changing lane.
Everyday word for the indicators. Literally 'arrows'.
All four indicators flashing together.
Also 'segnale acustico' or 'clacson'.
Sounding the horn.
Full beam. 'Lampeggiare con gli abbaglianti' = flash your headlights.
The normal headlights that do not dazzle others.
The mirrors you use to look behind you.
The space you keep behind the vehicle in front, so you can stop in time.
The space at the side between your vehicle and the one you pass.
Where a road crosses a railway line.
The gates or bars at a level crossing.
Red, amber (yellow) and green lights.
A police officer who directs traffic with signals.
Also 'passaggio pedonale' or 'strisce pedonali' (zebra crossing).
Same as 'attraversamento pedonale'.
A person walking.
A vehicle on rails in the street.
A bus powered by overhead electric wires.
A raised platform in the road where tram or bus passengers get on and off.
A bus on a fixed public route.
Bicycle, moped or motorbike.
A motorbike.
Carts pulled by horses or other animals.
A towed living trailer.
A fast road with separate carriageways and no junctions on the level.
A road outside built-up areas.
Inside a town or village. Lower speed limits apply.
The maximum speeds allowed.
Police, ambulance or fire vehicle with blue lights and siren on.
Following very close behind another vehicle.

terms.en: to queue up behind / follow closely
terms.note: To get in line right behind another vehicle.

terms.en: to move back in (to the right lane)
terms.note: Going back to your lane after overtaking.

terms.en: to cut in / cut someone off
terms.note: Moving in front of another vehicle too close, forcing it to brake.
Speeding up to compete with another vehicle.
Common in exam questions: 'deve accertarsi che…' = must make sure that…
A key word. 'È vietato' = it is forbidden.
A key word. 'È consentito' = it is allowed.
Something you must do. 'Ha l'obbligo di' = must.
TRAP WORD: statements with 'sempre' (always) are often false.
TRAP WORD: statements with 'mai' (never) are often false.
TRAP WORD: 'only' makes a statement narrow and often false.
Means the rule has exceptions.
Small word that changes the meaning: 'anche se' = even if.
Introduces a condition. Check if the condition really makes it legal.
